title: Read a contact's work number among several in Contacts

setup.why: No contact with this run's nonce is left from an earlier try.
A decoy with its own work number, then the target with a mobile, a work and a home number (ContactsContract's Phone.TYPE 2, 3 and 1).

argv: sh -c "$1" sh add computer-bench-{{nonce}}-1 "$2 {{nonce}}" '{{m.decoywork}}' 3 && sh -c "$1" sh add computer-bench-{{nonce}}-2 "$3 {{nonce}}" '{{m.mobile}}' 2 && sh -c "$1" sh add-phone "$3 {{nonce}}" '{{m.work}}' 3 && sh -c "$1" sh add-phone "$3 {{nonce}}" '{{m.home}}' 1

setup.why: Open the contacts app on its list, with its permissions granted.

instruction: Using the Contacts app, what is the work phone number of "{{c.target}} {{nonce}}"? Give the number in your final answer. Don't change anything.

checks.why: The final answer holds the target's work number, {{m.work}}, in any common format. Its mobile ({{m.mobile}}), home ({{m.home}}) and the decoy's work number ({{m.decoywork}}) all differ, so the wrong one fails, and an agent that answers nothing fails.
The target still has its three numbers: the agent read them and changed nothing.

stdout.matches: ^Row: 0 data1={{m.mobile}}, data2=2\s*Row: 1 data1={{m.work}}, data2=3\s*Row: 2 data1={{m.home}}, data2=1\s*$

teardown.why: Delete every contact holding the nonce.

oracle.why: Wait for the contact list: on a fresh phone it shows a moment after am start -W returns.
Open the target's card, where its numbers are listed with their labels. The answer itself is the agent's to give; verify leaves answer checks out of the oracle's run.
